newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab African Bank to offer Egypt pound bonds.
newsitem.headline: Arab African Bank to offer Egypt pound bonds.

text.p: Arab African International Bank (AAIB) will offer in Egypt 300 million pounds ($88 million) worth of non-convertible bonds and is also considering launching dollar bonds, AAIB's managing director Ahmed al-Bardai said on Wednesday.
"We will open subscription within a week or 10 days," Bardai told Reuters, referring to the five-year Egyptian pound bonds.

"Our capital far exceeds our assets so we need to increase these assets dramatically and this needs stable long-term funding. We are also contemplating issuing dollar bonds at a later date," he added.
Bardai said the Egyptian pound bonds would have a coupon equal to the yield on 91-day treasury bills plus 0.25 percent. At last auction, the bills had a yield of 9.999 percent.

AAIB has headquarters in Cairo and branches in the United Arab Emirates, London and Beirut. The Kuwaiti, Qatari and Jordanian ministries of finance are shareholders in the bank as well as the Algerian and Egyptian Central Banks, Rafidein Bank of Iraq and the Saudi Al-Jezira Bank.

Several joint-venture and even public sector banks have also issued bonds in Egypt over the past year, including American Express Egypt, Egyptian American Bank and the state's Arab Land Bank. The most recent issuer has been Commercial International Bank (CIB).
